conflicts.fact: Electron configuration notation and the number of electrons in the outer shell of Cl and Ar (third shell capacity)
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 teaches s/p notation (Na: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s¹), with Aufbau order including 4s, but then instructs students to draw Bohr diagrams with 'shell 3 holds max 8' for the 20 elements; Lesson 5 uses shell notation (2,8,1) and says Ca is 2,8,8,2. These are consistent with each other. However Lesson 5 claims Cl- achieves a stable '2,8,8' and Na+ is '2,8', whereas Lesson 5's Observe states sodium ends with 10 electrons and chlorine 18, consistent. No real conflict here beyond notation change.

conflicts.fact: Dimensions/number of groups of the grid and which elements sit as neighbours of the puzzle pairs
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the 20 elements form a grid of groups and periods and uses He/Ne, Li/Na, F/Cl as pairs, and that 'neighbouring elements can be completely different' (e.g. He and Li). Lesson 3 uses Na/K and Ne/Ar pairs and describes Cl and Ar as 'neighbours' behaving differently, a different dataset for the same puzzle.

conflicts.fact: What Lesson 1 learners sorted by / what the Lesson 1 card showed
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 overview says groups sorted by mass, reactivity or Kenyan context, but Observed says by atomic number, reactivity, state at room temperature and context. Lesson 2 says the Lesson 1 groupings were mass, reactivity or appearance and recalls 'four different groupings'.

conflicts.fact: What the Lesson 1 model artefact was
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 Model Version 1 is a blank-grid sketch plus a 'Model Panel' of what is inside two elements; Lesson 2 says the Lesson 1 model sketch showed how learners would arrange a subset of 10 cards.

conflicts.fact: Whether the learner element cards carried atomic number/mass etc. vs. Lesson 3 predictions with only atomic number, and element identities; also Lesson 1 says names are withheld ('you will earn those names') while Lesson 1 captions reveal Lithium, Sodium, Chlorine, Calcium
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 cards are 'unlabelled — no element names, no symbols' but the example captions are headed 'Card 3 — Lithium', 'Card 11 — Sodium' and the teacher says names will not be given yet; Lesson 3 cards are named Na, K, Ne, Ar.

Lesson 1: Card 20 is Calcium, Card 17 is Chlorine, Card 11 is Sodium (cards numbered 1–20 on the back, which would be atomic numbers); Lesson 7 uses the same numbering (consistent) — but Lesson 1 says cards numbered 1–20 'on the back only' while Lesson 7 projects 'Card 11'/'Card 17' with photographs, no conflict.

conflicts.fact: Which element appears in lessons for Group numbering: Group 17 vs 'Group VII', Group 18 vs 'Group VIII/0', and oxygen's group
conflicts.versions: Lessons 3 and 1 use Group I/VII/VIII (0); Lessons 4, 6 use Groups 1, 2, 16, 17, 18. Naming convention changes.

conflicts.fact: Lesson numbering of the unit length and which lesson the 'Six lessons in' statement refers to
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 teacher says 'Six lessons in' (correct), Lesson 6 Observe uses ion diagrams from Lesson 5; Lesson 5's closing says valency will be introduced 'next lesson' which fits. Lesson 8 says the full annotated poster is produced in Lesson 10 while Lesson 9 says the chain model is for the Lesson 10 gallery walk, a different artefact.

conflicts.fact: When the valency table was built
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 teacher says 'your valency table from yesterday' and 'the table you built yesterday', while Lesson 7 predict also describes it as 'the valency table they built in Lesson 6' - consistent; however Lesson 6 Cl₂O example states Cl has variable oxidation numbers in some compounds while Lesson 6 Learned says Group 17 → −1 fixed.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson answers the DQB question about 'how do we know which oxidation number to use' and which lesson answers the next question
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 says the 'what do we do when two compounds react' question is labelled 'Lesson 8 will answer this'; Lesson 8's new question is about conservation of mass, and the reaction question isn't addressed. Lesson 8 also states the Lesson 7 note asked 'How do we know which oxidation number to use?' whereas Lesson 6 posted that question.

conflicts.fact: Direction of reactivity trend and who answers it
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 promises the next two lessons will explain why reactivity increases down Group 1 and decreases down Group 17; Lesson 5 only displays them as open questions; Lesson 9 still lists the Group 1 question as open to be answered with the Nakuru scenario.

conflicts.fact: Element card assignment: how element cards were assigned/held
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 says one element per student was assigned in Lesson 3 while Lesson 3 has pairs taking back their own cards; Lesson 8 says the sodium card diagram was drawn or pasted in Lesson 3.

conflicts.fact: Rust and iron oxide oxidation state
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 anchors rust at Kisumu Port as Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ variable; Lesson 8 uses iron reacting with oxygen to form iron(III) oxide for Kisumu Port railings, consistent. Lesson 1 describes iron card as 'a Kisumu metalworks', a different Kisumu context.
